fullPassage:
Sweet Success: Lemonade Stand Economics

Author: Luke Peres
President of The Helpers, the school's biggest volunteer club

High school is not only where we study different subjects but also where we learn about life. We are a group of students that get together every week to discuss ways to make a difference in our society. In this newsletter, I would like to share the story of how we participated in our community's international food festival. On top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan. Here is our story.

Setting Up Our Plans
Choosing What to Sell:
The first step we took was to decide what to sell. Some of the ideas that we discussed included cotton candy, corn dogs, and lemonade. Out of these options, we agreed that a lemonade stand would be the easiest for us, as we would need only a good recipe and a few ingredients. We also found out that no other stand had signed up to sell drinks, so lemonade seemed to be the natural choice.

Finding the Perfect Recipe:
Once we decided on lemonade, we needed the perfect recipe. Fortunately, we were able to find a simple one online. We just needed freshly squeezed lemons, sugar, water, and ice. After trying out different variations of the recipe on friends and family, we decided on the final recipe. It would make about 1.5 liters of lemonade, which could be sold as five cups.

Pricing
The main goal of setting up the lemonade stand was to make enough profit for a donation to the local children's home. To maximize our profit, we needed to decrease our costs and increase our revenue.

Costs:
Since we wanted to minimize costs, our first step was to find the most affordable ingredients and cups available. As we were researching prices, we found that buying ingredients and cups in bulk would be the smartest way to go.

Revenue and Profit:
Now that we had found out how to minimize costs, we needed to decide on a reasonable price for a cup of lemonade. We contacted a festival organizer to gather information. First, we inquired about the previous year's drink prices, and she told us that soft drinks had been sold for $1.50 per cup. Considering that freshly squeezed lemonade usually costs more, we decided to sell each cup for $2. Based on our recipe and the costs of the ingredients and cups, each cup of lemonade would cost us about $0.70 to make. With a selling price of $2, we expected a profit of $1.30 per cup.

Regarding attendance, we learned that the festival organizers were expecting around 400 people for each of the two days of the festival. We thought we could reasonably sell lemonade to half of the people attending, so we aimed to sell 400 cups over the two days. If we could do that, our revenue would amount to $800!

However, this revenue wouldn't be pure profit. We needed to subtract our costs from it. In addition to the cost of $280 required to make 400 cups, we also had to factor in the $6 we needed for posters and fliers. If we reached our goal, we would be able to make $514 in profit. That would be a big donation!

Marketing
Location-Based Marketing:
When the organizer asked us where we wanted our stand, we knew that location was going to be important. She sent us a map showing which foods were going to be sold at which stands, and we chose an opening between the tteokbokki and spicy kebab stands. Who could resist a cool, sweet lemonade after some spicy and salty food?

Our Marketing Strategies:
Developing marketing strategies to attract more customers was the most enjoyable part. In addition to designing posters and fliers, we also explored various online marketing techniques. One of our club members suggested we offer customers free refills for mentioning our stand on their social media accounts. We all agreed that was a great way to spread the word. We also planned to install a photo zone and give coupons for a 10% discount to customers who posted photos they took there with the tag "#sweetsuccess," the name of our stand.

The Results
Mission completed! Our lemonade stand was a huge success! Because of the hot weather, we ended up purchasing extra bags of ice. We also had to give free refills and discounts to some customers, which we did as part of our marketing strategy. Even with these extra costs, however, we were still able to make a profit of $479. Even though we couldn't reach our profit goal, we were happy that we were able to make a big donation to the children's home. We also learned a valuable lesson in economics, a lesson we never could have learned in the classroom!

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 'how to create and carry out'에서 and는 create와 carry를 병렬 연결하므로 carry(동사원형)가 맞다. carrying은 틀림.
det.analysis:
✅ ① get: 주어 students에 수일치, 복수 → get 정상
✅ ② participated: 과거 시제, 축제에 참여했다
✅ ③ raising: 전치사 on top of + -ing (동명사)
❌ ④ carrying → carry: 'how to create and carry out'에서 to부정사 병렬
det.tip: how to V1 and V2: to부정사 병렬은 둘 다 원형. on top of + -ing: 전치사 뒤 동명사.

det.korean: ④ 'seemed to be'가 원문이므로 to be가 맞다. being은 틀림. seem 뒤에는 to부정사.
det.analysis:

✅ ② easiest: the + 최상급, 'the easiest for us'
✅ ③ signed: had signed up (과거완료)
❌ ④ being → to be: seem + to부정사 구문
det.tip: seem + to V: ~인 것 같다. seem being (X), seem to be (O). seem은 to부정사를 취하는 동사.

det.analysis:

✅ ② had been sold: 과거완료 수동태 (전년도 일이므로 대과거)
✅ ③ Considering: 분사구문/접속사적 용법 '~을 고려하면'
❌ ④ selling → to sell: decide + to V (to부정사 목적어)
det.tip: decide + to V: decide selling (X), decide to sell (O). 유사: want/hope/plan + to V.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'That would be a big donation!'으로 끝남. 관계대명사로 수식할 경우 선행사 donation이 있으므로 that/which가 맞다. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 틀림.
det.analysis:
✅ ① attending: 현재분사 (people attending = 참석하는 사람들)
✅ ② required: 과거분사 (cost required to make = 만드는 데 필요한 비용)
✅ ③ reached: 가정법 과거 (If + 과거, would + 원형)
❌ ④ what → that/which: 선행사 donation이 있으므로 관계대명사 what 불가
det.tip: what vs that/which: what = the thing that (선행사 포함). 선행사가 있으면 that/which 사용.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'subtract(빼다)'인데 'add(더하다)'로 바뀌었다. 순수익을 구하려면 비용을 빼야 하므로 add는 문맥상 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① affordable(저렴한): 원문 일치. 비용 최소화를 위해 저렴한 재료
✅ ② profit(이익): 원문 일치. 판매가 - 원가 = 이익
✅ ③ revenue(수입): 원문 일치. 매출액
❌ ④ add(더하다) → subtract(빼다): 매출에서 비용을 '빼야' 순이익
det.tip: subtract(빼다) ↔ add(더하다). revenue - costs = profit.

questions.passage: When the organizer asked us where we wanted our stand, we knew that location was going to be important. She sent us a map showing which foods were going to be sold at which stands, and we chose an opening between the tteokbokki and spicy kebab stands. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'spread(퍼뜨리다)'인데 'limit(제한하다)'로 바뀌었다. 소문을 퍼뜨리는 마케팅 전략이므로 limit은 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① resist(저항하다): 원문 일치. '누가 거부할 수 있겠는가'
✅ ② attract(끌어들이다): 원문 일치. 고객을 유치하다
✅ ③ mentioning(언급하다): 원문 일치. SNS에서 가게를 언급
❌ ④ limit(제한하다) → spread(퍼뜨리다): 'spread the word' = 소문을 퍼뜨리다
det.tip: spread the word(소문을 퍼뜨리다) ↔ limit the word(말을 제한하다). 마케팅 맥락에서는 spread가 적절.

위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"다른 부스에서 이미 음료를 판매하기로 등록해 두었다."

det.korean: F. 원문: 'no other stand had signed up to sell drinks' — 다른 부스에서 음료를 판매하기로 등록한 곳은 없었다.
det.analysis: 진술문은 '이미 등록해 두었다'고 했으나, 원문은 'no other stand had signed up'으로 정반대. F.
det.tip: no other stand = 다른 부스 없음. 부정 표현을 정확히 파악해야 T/F 판별 가능.

det.analysis: $0.70 = 제조 원가, $1.30 = 이익 (판매가 $2 - 원가 $0.70). 진술문의 $1.30은 이익이지 원가가 아님. F.
det.tip: 숫자 함정: cost($0.70)와 profit($1.30)을 혼동하지 않도록 주의.

"최종 이익은 목표했던 금액을 초과 달성했다."

det.korean: F. 원문: 'Even though we couldn't reach our profit goal' — 이익 목표($514)에 도달하지 못했다. 실제 이익은 $479.
det.analysis: 목표 $514 vs 실제 $479. '초과 달성'이 아니라 미달. F.
det.tip: couldn't reach our goal = 목표에 도달하지 못했다. 초과 달성과 정반대.

questions.passage: The main goal of setting up the lemonade stand was to make enough profit for a donation to the local children's home. To maximize our profit, we needed to decrease our costs and increase our revenue. Since we wanted to minimize costs, our first step was to find the most __________ ingredients and cups available. As we were researching prices, we found that buying ingredients and cups in bulk would be the smartest way to go. We contacted a festival organizer to gather information.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비용을 최소화하려면 가장 저렴한(affordable) 재료와 컵을 찾아야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① affordable(저렴한): 원문 일치. minimize costs → affordable
❌ ② expensive(비싼): 비용 최소화와 반대
❌ ③ organic(유기농): 비용 절감과 무관
❌ ④ imported(수입된): 비용 절감과 무관
det.tip: affordable = 가격이 알맞은, 감당할 수 있는. minimize costs(비용 최소화)의 맥락.

questions.passage: When the organizer asked us where we wanted our stand, we knew that location was going to be important. She sent us a map showing which foods were going to be sold at which stands, and we chose an opening between the tteokbokki and spicy kebab stands. Who could resist a cool, sweet lemonade after some spicy and salty food? Developing marketing strategies to attract more customers was the most enjoyable part. We also planned to install a photo zone and give coupons for a 10% discount to customers who posted photos with the tag "#sweetsuccess." The students understood that __________ was key to increasing sales at the festival.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: reducing the number of festival days

det.korean: 매출 증대의 핵심은 전략적 위치 선정과 적극적인 홍보(strategic location and active promotion)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 본문은 위치 선정(떡볶이/케밥 사이)과 마케팅 전략(SNS, 포토존, 쿠폰)을 핵심으로 다룸
❌ ① 품질 낮추기: 본문에 언급 없음
❌ ② 가격 인상: 합리적 가격 설정이 주제
❌ ④ 축제 일수 줄이기: 본문과 무관
det.tip: Marketing 단락의 핵심: 위치(location-based) + 온라인 홍보(SNS, 포토존, 쿠폰).

questions.passage: Once we decided on lemonade, we needed the perfect recipe. Fortunately, we were able to find a simple one online. We just needed freshly squeezed lemons, sugar, water, and ice. After trying out different variations of the recipe on friends and family, we decided on the final recipe. It would make about 1.5 liters of lemonade, which could be sold as five cups.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 레시피를 직접 개발하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸렸다.
최종 레시피로 약 1.5리터의 레모네이드를 만들 수 있었다.
친구와 가족에게 레시피를 시험해 보지 않았다.
레모네이드 한 배치로 열 잔을 판매할 수 있었다.

det.korean: ② 원문: 'It would make about 1.5 liters of lemonade, which could be sold as five cups.' 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 1.5리터, 5잔: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ① 온라인에서 간단한 레시피를 찾았다고 함 (직접 개발 X)
❌ ③ 'trying out different variations on friends and family' — 시험해 봄
❌ ④ 5잔이지 10잔이 아님
det.tip: 수치 확인: 1.5 liters = five cups. 열 잔(ten cups)은 오답.

questions.passage: Regarding attendance, we learned that the festival organizers were expecting around 400 people for each of the two days of the festival. We thought we could reasonably sell lemonade to half of the people attending, so we aimed to sell 400 cups over the two days. If we could do that, our revenue would amount to $800! However, this revenue wouldn't be pure profit. We needed to subtract our costs from it. In addition to the cost of $280 required to make 400 cups, we also had to factor in the $6 we needed for posters and fliers. If we reached our goal, we would be able to make $514 in profit.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 축제에는 이틀간 총 400명이 방문할 것으로 예상되었다.

det.korean: ① 원문: 'around 400 people for each of the two days' — 하루에 400명씩, 이틀이면 총 800명. '총 400명'은 불일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 하루 400명 × 2일 = 총 800명. '총 400명'은 틀림
✅ ② $2 × 400잔 = $800: 원문 일치
✅ ③ $280 for 400 cups: 원문 일치
✅ ④ $6 for posters and fliers: 원문 일치
det.tip: '400 people for each of the two days' = 매일 400명. 총 참석자 = 800명. 판매 목표는 절반인 400잔.

questions.passage: (a) Fortunately, we were able to find a simple one online. (b) We just needed freshly squeezed lemons, sugar, water, and ice. (c) As we were researching prices, we found that buying ingredients and cups in bulk would be the smartest way to go. (d) We contacted a festival organizer to gathering information about the previous year's drink prices.
questions.stem: 위 (a)~(d) 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?

det.korean: (d) 'to gathering' → 'to gather': to부정사 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (a)
❌ ② (b)
✅ ③ (c)
❌ ④ (d)
✅ (a) were able to find: 정상
✅ (b) needed + 명사 나열: 정상
✅ (c) found that + 주어 + 동사: 명사절 정상
❌ (d) to gathering → to gather: to부정사(목적) = to + 동사원형
det.tip: to + V(원형): 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법. to gathering(X), to gather(O).

questions.passage: The main goal of setting up the lemonade stand was to make enough profit for a donation to the local children's home. To maximize our profit, we needed to decrease our costs and increase our revenue.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"이익을 극대화하기 위해 비용을 줄이고 (          )을/를 늘려야 했다."

det.korean: 이익 극대화를 위해 비용을 줄이고 수입(revenue)을 늘려야 했다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'decrease our costs and increase our revenue.' 빈칸은 '수입'에 해당하는 revenue.
det.tip: revenue(수입, 매출) ↔ costs(비용). maximize profit = decrease costs + increase revenue.

questions.passage: We also found out that no other stand had signed up to sell drinks, so lemonade seemed to be the natural choice. In addition to designing posters and fliers, we also explored various online marketing techniques. questions.passage: High school is not only where we study different subjects but also where we learn about life. We are a group of students that get together every week to discuss ways to make a difference in our society. In this newsletter, I would like to share the story of how we participated in our community's international food festival. On top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan. Here is our story.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 봉사 활동을 통해 사업 계획을 세우고 실행하며 배운 경험
국제 음식 축제에서 인기 있는 음식의 종류
기부를 위한 모금 활동의 법적 절차

det.korean: 글의 주제: 봉사 클럽이 축제 참여를 통해 사업 계획을 세우고 실행하며 배운 경험.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 본문 전체의 핵심: 기부 목적 레모네이드 사업 → 계획/가격/마케팅/결과 → 경제 수업
❌ ① 과목 공부 방법: 글의 부분적 배경일 뿐
❌ ③ 축제 인기 음식: 글의 주제 아님
❌ ④ 법적 절차: 글에 언급 없음
det.tip: 도입부 + 마무리 확인: '사업 계획 수립·실행' + '교실에서 배울 수 없는 경제 수업'.

questions.passage: Mission completed! Our lemonade stand was a huge success! Because of the hot weather, we ended up purchasing extra bags of ice. We also had to give free refills and discounts to some customers, which we did as part of our marketing strategy. Even with these extra costs, however, we were still able to make a profit of $479. Even though we couldn't reach our profit goal, we were happy that we were able to make a big donation to the children's home. We also learned a valuable lesson in economics, a lesson we never could have learned in the classroom!
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 사업에서 목표 이익을 달성하지 못하면 실패이다.
더운 날씨는 음료 판매에 항상 유리하게 작용한다.
목표에 미치지 못했지만 기부와 경제적 교훈이라는 가치 있는 성과를 얻었다.
마케팅 비용을 줄이면 순이익을 극대화할 수 있다.

det.korean: 요지: 목표 이익($514)에는 미달했지만, 큰 기부와 경제 수업이라는 소중한 성과를 얻었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 핵심: 목표 미달($479 < $514)이지만 기부 + 교실 밖 경제 교훈
❌ ① '실패'라고 보지 않음 — happy, huge success라고 표현
❌ ② 더운 날씨는 추가 비용(얼음) 발생의 원인이기도 함
❌ ④ 마케팅 비용 절감이 주제가 아님
det.tip: 결론부의 핵심 표현: 'a valuable lesson in economics, a lesson we never could have learned in the classroom.'

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
"돈을 기부할 만큼 충분히 모금하는 것 외에도, 우리는 사업 계획을 세우고 실행하는 법을 많이 배웠다."
[조건] On top of / raising / create / carry out 를 사용할 것
questions.wa: On top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan.
accept: On top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan.
On top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan
on top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan

det.korean: 기부를 위한 충분한 모금 외에도, 사업 계획을 세우고 실행하는 법을 많이 배웠다.
det.analysis: On top of(~외에도) + raising(동명사) + enough money to make a donation(기부할 충분한 돈) + learned about how to create and carry out(세우고 실행하는 법)
det.tip: On top of = In addition to (~외에도). carry out = 실행하다, 수행하다.

questions.ans: On top of raising enough money to make a donation, we learned a lot about how to create and carry out a business plan.
